lines: Two Euclidean sequencers sharing one clock, each spreading a chosen number of filled steps as evenly as it can over a chosen length
Rotates sequence α around its own length, moving where the filled steps fall without changing how many there are; it shifts by none up to one step short of the length
Rotates sequence β around its own length, moving where the filled steps fall without changing how many there are; it shifts by none up to one step short of the length
Sets how many steps sequence α runs before it comes round again, 1 to 16
Sets how many steps sequence β runs before it comes round again, 1 to 16
Sets how many of sequence α's steps are filled, from one of them to all of them, spread as evenly over the length as the two numbers allow
Sets how many of sequence β's steps are filled, from one of them to all of them, spread as evenly over the length as the two numbers allow
Chooses whether the two sequences both advance on every clock, or take turns: α runs its whole length, then β runs its whole length, and while one is running both outputs carry it
Sets what the α output does on a filled step: hold 10V for the whole step, put out nothing, or repeat the clock pulse; the maker's tooltip calls the holding setting Alternating, which it is not
Sets what the β output does on a filled step: hold 10V for the whole step, put out nothing, or repeat the clock pulse; the maker's tooltip calls the holding setting Alternating, which it is not
A rising edge past 2V sends both sequences back to the step their rotation knob picks
Advances both sequences on each rising edge past 2V, and its high and low state is what the repeating setting of the mode switches passes on
Carries sequence α, 10V on a filled step and 0V otherwise, shaped by the α mode switch
Carries sequence β, 10V on a filled step and 0V otherwise, shaped by the β mode switch
Carries 10V for as long as the clock input is above its threshold and 0V below it
Note — nothing moves until a clock is patched; the module has no clock of its own
Note — while the two sequences are taking turns both outputs carry whichever one is running, so α and β put out the same thing
Note — on the hardware the mode switches double as a reset; in this version they do not

Stoicheia.notes: Mode A and Mode B are configSwitch(MODE_x_PARAM, LATCHED, NORMAL, NORMAL, ..., {"Alternating", "Mute", "Trigger"}) at Stoicheia.cpp:165-166, so the tooltip for the LATCHED position reads Alternating; the code at lines 234-238 holds the output at a flat 10V for the whole filled step, which is not alternation. Klasmata's latched mode does alternate, and the label looks to have come from there. The Sequence mode switch is drawn with rack's three-frame BefacoSwitch but configured 0 to 1, and SvgSwitch picks its frame as value minus minimum, so INDEPENDENT shows the lever down and ALTERNATING shows it centred; the lever never reaches the top position. The panel prints alpha-plus-beta below that switch and nothing above it, which could be read as marking the lower position, and the lower position is the independent one. That is worth checking in the rack before anybody relies on the marking. The panel prints no words at all apart from the two Greek letters, so no line carries a panel label.

Tonic.notes: The six offsets are fixed in the source at Tonic.cpp:28 as 0, 16, 8, 4, 2 and -1 semitones, the first of those replaced by the knob at line 72. The output is a sum of semitones, not a quantiser: nothing is fed in to be quantised, and the maker's own name for the jack, Quantized CV, describes the twelfth-of-a-volt grid rather than any quantising of an input. The panel prints GT and CV under the two output jacks and nothing at all beside the buttons.

lines: A Euclidean sequencer: it spreads a chosen number of filled steps as evenly as it can over a chosen length, and walks through them on a clock
Rotates the pattern around its length, moving where the filled steps fall without changing how many there are
Sets how many steps the sequence runs before it comes round again, 1 to 32
Sets what the output does: repeat the voltage at the clock input on a filled step, put out nothing, or flip a 10V gate over every time the pattern changes between filled and empty
Sets how many of the steps are filled, from one of them to all of them, spread as evenly over the length as the two numbers allow
Sets how much of the length CV reaches the length, none at the far left and its full 31 steps at the far right
Sets how much of the fill CV reaches the fill, none at the far left and the whole of the fill knob's travel at the far right
A rising edge past 2V sends the sequence back to the step the rotation knob picks
Shifts the length, 10V covering all 31 steps at full attenuation, added to the length knob and held between 1 and 32
Adds to the fill knob, 10V covering the whole of its travel at full attenuation, and the total is held between one filled step and all of them
Advances the sequence on each rising edge past 2V
Carries the sequence, shaped by the mode switch
Note — nothing moves until a clock is patched; the module has no clock of its own
Note — in the repeating setting the output copies the voltage present at the clock input rather than putting out a fixed 10V, so a 5V clock gives a 5V sequence
Note — on the hardware the mode switch doubles as a reset; in this version it does not

Klasmata.notes: Klasmata's mode enum is LATCHED, NORMAL, MUTE (Klasmata.cpp:90-94) with NORMAL the default, the opposite order to Stoicheia's, and its tooltip labels match the code. In the NORMAL setting line 192 puts out state times the clock input's own voltage, so the output level follows the clock rather than being a fixed 10V. In the LATCHED setting line 195 puts out a toggle that flips whenever the pattern changes between filled and empty, which is a divided gate rather than a step-long one. The panel prints no words, only the Greek letter gamma and a set of symbols, so no line carries a panel label.

lines: A free-running clock with a main output and two more that multiply or divide it
Sets the tempo of the main clock, 40 to 200 BPM
Divides or multiplies the main clock for the first of the two scaled outputs, stepping through divide by 8, 6, 4, 3 and 2, then times 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8
Divides or multiplies the main clock for the second of the two scaled outputs, stepping through divide by 24, 12, 8, 4 and 2, then times 1, 2, 4, 8, 12 and 24
Carries the main clock at the tempo the BPM knob sets, 10V high
Carries the first of the two scaled clocks, 10V high
Carries the second of the two scaled clocks, 10V high
Note — there is no clock input, so the module cannot be locked to anything else; it runs from its own BPM knob
Note — moving either scaling knob restarts that output in step with the main clock
Menu — Output multiplier: x1, x2, x4, x8, x16 — speeds up all three outputs together, so at x4 the module runs four times faster than the BPM knob reads
Menu — Trigger mode: Trigger, Gate, Original — sets the pulse length: Gate half the output's own cycle, Trigger a forty-eighth of a main-clock cycle, Original half the cycle capped at half a main one

CLK.notes: The two scaling tables are literals at CLK.cpp:13-16. The master runs at 48 ticks per main-clock cycle (line 194), and the three trigger modes set the pulse length through maxDuty at lines 198-210: Gate uses INT16_MAX so duty always comes out as half the period, Original uses 24 ticks, and Trigger uses max(1, (1e-3/tickTime)/48), which only exceeds one tick above about 60000 BPM and so is always exactly one master tick in practice. The theme and default-theme menu items are cosmetic and every module in the plugin carries them, so they are not written as lines.

lines: A clock divider on one side, a clock counter or clock delay on the other, and a fourth output that combines the two
Sets the division: 1, then every even number up to 64
In the counting setting, sets how many clocks pass between pulses, 1 to 32; in the delay setting, sets the delay, 0 to 1000ms; in the off setting it does nothing
Sets how much of the division CV reaches the division knob, none at the far left and the whole of its travel at the far right
Sets how much of the count-or-delay CV reaches that knob, none at the far left and the whole of its travel at the far right
Chooses what the right-hand side does: count clocks, delay them, or nothing, and in the off setting the division, count and combined outputs are all held at 0V
Adds to the division knob, 10V covering the whole of its travel at full attenuation
Adds to the count-or-delay knob, 10V covering the whole of its travel at full attenuation
A rising edge past 1V restarts the divider, the counter and the delay together
Advances the divider, the counter and the delay on each rising edge past 1V
A square wave at the divided rate, flipping between 0V and 10V each time the division count comes round; set to 1 it repeats the clock instead of halving it
In the counting setting, 10V for one clock each time the count comes round; in the delay setting, the clock pulse repeated after the set delay
In the counting setting, a pulse once the counter has counted that many of the divider's changes; in the delay setting, the clock with pulses landing on a divider change pushed late, giving a swing
Carries 10V for as long as the clock input is above its threshold and 0V below it
Note — nothing moves until a clock is patched; the module has no clock of its own
Note — the delay is worked out in blocks of 64 samples rather than one sample at a time, so the delayed edge lands to the nearest block

Logoi.notes: Logoi's clock and reset jacks use rack's default Schmitt thresholds of 1V and 0V, not the 2V and 0.1V that Stoicheia, Klasmata and Phoreo use. The division knob maps to 1 or any even number from 2 to 64 through divisionFromParamUser at line 367; the division output is a toggle, so a setting of 2 flips it on alternate clocks, while the setting of 1 is a special case that passes the clock gate straight through. The mode switch is configSwitch(MODE_PARAM, 0, 2, 0, "Mode", {"Count", "Delay", "Off"}), and the maker's own comments at lines 347-348 say Count is the switch down and Delay the switch middle. The panel prints no name beside that switch. The delay clocks are ticked once every 64 samples (updateClocksFrequency, line 233).

lines: Three stages on one clock: it reshapes the pulse width, multiplies the rate, and repeats each trigger a set number of times
Sets the pulse width as a share of the incoming clock's period, 0 to 100%, and the same share is applied to all three outputs
Sets how much of the pulse width CV reaches that knob, none at the far left and the whole of its travel at the far right
Sets how many pulses the multiplier puts out for each clock it receives, 1 to 16
Sets how much of the multiplier CV reaches that knob, none at the far left and its full 16 steps at the far right
Sets how many times each incoming trigger is repeated, 1 to 16, spaced at whatever rate the multiplier is running
Sets how much of the repeat CV reaches that knob, none at the far left and its full 16 steps at the far right
The clock whose pulse width is reshaped; its period is measured between rising edges past 2V
Adds to the pulse width knob, 10V covering the whole of its travel at full attenuation
The clock the multiplier subdivides, taken on rising edges past 2V; with nothing patched it uses the clock above it
Adds to the multiplier knob, 10V covering its full 16 steps at full attenuation
The trigger that fires a burst of repeats, taken on rising edges past 2V; with nothing patched it uses whichever clock the multiplier is using
Adds to the repeat knob, 10V covering its full 16 steps at full attenuation
The incoming clock with its pulse width reset by the pulse width knob, 10V high
The multiplied clock, 10V high
A burst of repeats each time a trigger arrives, 10V high
Note — the multiplier measures the period between two clock edges, so the first cycle after a clock starts is not divided up
Note — with only the top jack patched all three stages run from it, because the second input is normalled to the first and the third to the second
